Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> Football U-23 AFCONQ: Black Meteors stun Libya with injury-time winner to seal dramatic comeback Source : Daniel Koranteng 17 November 2026 5:30pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
Denis Marfo's injury-time penalty handed Ghana's Black Meteors a dramatic 3-1 victory over Libya in the second leg of their CAF U-23 Africa Cup of Nations qualifier, securing a 3-2 aggregate win and progression to the next round.
Trailing 1-0 from the first leg in Benghazi, Ghana made a bright start and took the lead in the 20th minute through a fine close-range finish from Lord Afrifa.
Desmond Ofei's side continued to dominate proceedings and came close to doubling their advantage on several occasions, but poor finishing and some impressive goalkeeping kept the Libyans in the game.
However, a lapse in concentration on the stroke of half-time allowed Libya to equalise, leaving Ghana needing two more goals to advance under the away-goal rule.
The second half saw the Black Meteors desperately searching for a breakthrough, but clear-cut chances were few and far between.
Ghana eventually found their second in the 63rd minute after winning a free-kick about 35 yards from goal. Aaron Essel produced a moment of brilliance, curling a powerful effort past the Libyan goalkeeper to put the hosts 2-1 ahead.
The Black Meteors continued to push for the decisive third goal and were rewarded in the fourth minute of injury time when the referee awarded a penalty following a foul on Essel.
Marfo stepped up and sent the goalkeeper the wrong way, sealing a 3-1 win on the night and a 3-2 victory on aggregate.

The dramatic comeback was, however, overshadowed by ugly scenes after the final whistle, as players and officials from both sides clashed in a series of confrontations, marring the end of what had been a fiercely contested encounter.
Ghana progresses to the third and final qualifying round, where seven two-legged ties will determine the teams joining hosts Egypt at the 2027 finals.
The tournament will also form part of Africa’s qualification pathway for the men’s football competition at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games.
